Voatdev

Last week in /v/voatdev began with a question about the block feature. At present it only collapses comments, not posts, or at least as far as I know.

Next was a question about whether or not Voat is still being developed. The only response was one citing Putt's burnout. While that remains a factor, I feel the need to point out that things weren't the most bustling last summer either, and where massive-scale projects managed entirely from one person's free time are concerned, I don't see anything surprising about that. I will also point out that the most active Putt has been in recent years (at least from an observer's point of view) was last autumn and winter, when the testing for the Port began, along with combating the biggest DDoS Voat has yet experienced. Perhaps this autumn, too, things will pick up again. In the meantime, Voat's activity has been stable these past several months.

There was also a suggestion for DDoS protection last week. I have no idea how reliable or trustworthy the proposed protection is.

Next was a strange post where Voat's publicly available code seems to have been used to host a pseudo-Voat in order to do testing, and in which suggestions for efficient banning of spammers were laid out. I think.

Finally, there was a report about links submissions to mp4s and webms from specific hosts not producing thumbnails, allegedly for almost a year now. I have not noticed such an absence, but then again specific links types on specific hosts are not easy to search for on Voat, unless I were to search by domain and try to find a post that goes to an mp4, and I don't have the time or inclination to post such a link myself presently. Maybe it's a bug, maybe it's a troll.
